title: The Connection Editorial Standard
purpose: A global, interdisciplinary knowledge atlas that explains subjects accurately and makes their relationships discoverable.
principles: Clear distinction between established findings, interpretation and uncertainty
Original concise explanations rather than copied source text
Connections must explain a real relationship, not merely share a category

contentStatuses.starter: Template-based introduction. Substantive research and rewriting required.
contentStatuses.review-pending: Entry exists but has not passed a documented editorial review.
contentStatuses.reviewed: A named review pass checked factual claims, dates, wording and references.
contentStatuses.needs-update: Previously reviewed entry needs checking because evidence or context may have changed.
contentStatuses.research-enriched: Entry rewritten or expanded against named references; still awaiting independent subject-expert review.

sourceRequirements.baseline: At least two independent, subject-specific sources for reviewed entries where practical.
preferred: Primary documents and official datasets for original records and statistics
Peer-reviewed research and academic books for specialist scientific claims
Universities, national academies, museums, archives and public institutions for specialist explainers and collections
Established reference works for orientation, not as the sole basis for contested claims
avoid: A broad field overview presented as evidence for a narrow specialist topic
Unverified social posts or anonymous pages
Treating the presence of a link as proof that every sentence is correct

connectionRequirements: Every connection must have a meaningful, readable explanation.
Prefer causal, historical, methodological, conceptual or practical relationships.
Do not add reciprocal duplicates unless direction changes the meaning.
Avoid connecting topics solely because they share a collection.
For important foundational subjects, add cross-disciplinary links where the relationship can be explained accurately.
reviewWorkflow: Define the scope and key questions for the subject.
Consult independent sources and record their specific contribution.
Write an original explanation in plain language.
Check names, dates, units, definitions and uncertainty.
Review links and explain each important relationship.
Set contentStatus to reviewed only after the checks are documented.
editorialBoundaries: Do not label a source as peer-reviewed unless verified.
Do not invent dates, citations, quotations or statistics.
Distinguish consensus from active scientific or historical debate.
